name: Abū Manṣūr Mawhūb ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Khaḍir al-Jawālīqī
summary: Lexicographer of Baghdad, pupil of al-Khaṭīb al-Tibrīzī, imam of the caliph al-Muqtafī, author of al-Muʿarrab on foreign words in Arabic; one of Ibn al-Anbārī's own teachers.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī, his pupil, calls al-Jawālīqī one of the great lexicographers, trustworthy and truthful, who took from al-Khaṭīb al-Tibrīzī and led the caliph al-Muqtafī in prayer.
He died in Baghdad in 539/1144. His al-Muʿarrab collects the foreign words that entered Arabic, and his Takmilat iṣlāḥ mā taghlaṭu fīhi al-ʿāmma corrects the mistakes of common speech.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 473–478
Cevâlîkī, Mevhûb b. Ahmed, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
